messages.subject: world map and Gini index
parts: Hey guys, I am really a beginner in the R software. I would like to ask you whether you can help me with my problem. messages.author: af271c8777c52f76
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] world map and Gini index
parts:
Dear Petra,

Working with the csv file you provided, the following works:
> orig = read.table('krajiny.csv', sep=';', dec=',', header=T, stringsAsFactors=F)
> sp = joinCountryData2Map(orig, joinCode="NAME", nameJoinColumn= "Country")
152 codes from your data successfully matched countries in the map
1 codes from your data failed to match with a country code in the map
91 codes from the map weren't represented in your data
> mapCountryData(sp, nameColumnToPlot="Gini")

This is a straightforward modification of the example given in the package vignette (section 2, "Mapping your own country data").
If you want to see which is the one country that failed, you have to perform the difference on two sets:
> data(countrySynonyms)
> allnames = unlist(countrySynonyms[,3:7], use.names=F)
> setdiff(orig$Country,allnames)
[1] "Congo-Brazzaville"

countrySynonyms is a dataset from rworldmap, giving "official" synonyms for country names.

Why is "Congo-Brazzaville" not understood by rworldmap? Because its official name is simply "Congo":
> grep("Congo",countrySynonyms$name1, value=T)
[1] "Congo"                               
[2] "Congo, The Democratic Republic of the"

The first above is Congo-Brazzaville, the second is the DRC, i.e. Congo-Kinshasa.

That's why using official 3-letter ISO codes (the norm is called ISO3166-1 alpha-3) is advisable.

Regards,
   JB

messages.author: af271c8777c52f76
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] world map and Gini index
parts:
By the way, you definitely have a naming problem in your file:

Congo;44,43
Congo-Brazzaville;40,17

This is why in the map the DRC is left blank: because "Congo" has been linked to the country which capital city is Brazzaville, while you seem to expect that the value 44.43 is linked to the DRC (ISO code "COD") and 40.17 to the Congo (ISO code "COG").

Cheers,
   JB
